name: Alex Hormozi
description: Turn the point into a rule the reader can act on today. Short lines, hard stops, a reversal at the end.
scope: His X posts from January to October 2026. It studies short rule posts, ranked lists and example-led explanations, not his books, videos, podcasts or paid courses.
strengths: Turning a lesson into a memorable rule
Motivating action with a blunt diagnosis and a fix
limitations: The certainty can sound preachy when the brief is a nuanced or sensitive topic.
Rules need a real lesson behind them; without one the post becomes a generic motivational line.

sources.title: The best way to accomplish your goals
sources.note: Setup and answer: a line ending in a colon names the goal, and a four-word answer on its own line overturns the expected advice.

sources.title: Focus beats intelligence
sources.note: A parallel stack of three lines with identical grammar, each pairing a virtue that wins against a more admired one.

sources.title: Most common reasons for failing, in order
sources.note: A ranked list numbered with closing brackets, each item a short phrase, ordered from never starting to aiming too low.

sources.title: You can boil success into focus and patience
sources.note: An equation with a plus sign, two urges mapped to their failures with arrows, a sentence of diagnosis and a closing reversal aimed at the reader.

sources.title: What to do when you're not sure what to do
sources.note: Rule, an "Ex:" line with five everyday hyphen examples in the same pattern, one sentence of mechanism, and a baseball metaphor ending in fragments.

sources.title: It always takes longer and costs more
sources.note: A list of three costs stated, then repeated and escalated in the second paragraph, so the repetition itself makes the argument.

sources.title: Customers become friends faster than friends become customers
sources.note: A single-sentence reversal in which the two halves swap places, the whole post being the rule.

sources.title: 80% done is only a third of the way there
sources.note: Corrects a number people trust with two quoted percentages, then lands on two short lines, the last one using mild profanity.

sources.title: Outlandish success and unbalanced effort
sources.note: Intense diction about effort over a long time span, followed by a closing run of clipped imperatives.

observations.trait: Posts follow a few fixed shapes: setup and answer, parallel stack, ranked list, equation, or rule with examples.
Reversals carry the punch: the second half of a line overturns or mirrors the first.
Repetition and escalation replace argument; the same items return stronger.
Short lines and fragments end the post with clipped imperatives or a sports metaphor.
Numbers correct intuition or describe effort rather than show off.
